TX-senate.statusNote: Nominees set: Ken Paxton (R) won the May 26 runoff over Sen. John Cornyn; James Talarico (D) won the March primary.

TX-governor.statusNote: Nominees set in the March 3 primary: Gov. Greg Abbott (R) and state Rep. Gina Hinojosa (D).

candidates.name: Ken Paxton
candidates.background: Texas Attorney General since 2015. Won the May 2026 Republican runoff against Sen. John Cornyn. Impeached by the Texas House in 2023 and acquitted by the Senate.

health.label: Led lawsuit to strike down the entire Affordable Care Act (Wikipedia)

immigration.label: Campaign: secure border, deportations; challenged DACA; defended SB4; backed border wall (Wikipedia)

climate.label: Sued EPA over Clean Power Plan; defended ExxonMobil in climate probes (Wikipedia)

repro.label: Enforced Texas abortion bans; sued FDA over mifepristone; opposed Kate Cox exemption (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Filed Texas v. Pennsylvania challenging 2020 results; ran voter-fraud unit; defended voter ID (Wikipedia)

cost.label: Campaign: 'cut taxes and stop the wasteful spending' and 'remove harmful regulations' to lower costs (Paxton campaign)

education.label: Campaign pledges to 'protect parental rights' in schools; attacks 'radical gender ideology' content (Paxton campaign)

safety.label: Created AG human-trafficking unit and won quadrupled enforcement funding; led Backpage raid (Wikipedia)

housing.label: As AG issued an August 2020 opinion that local governments cannot 'prohibit, delay, or restrict' eviction notices, blocking pandemic eviction moratoriums (Texas Tribune)

controversies.title: Securities-fraud case
controversies.detail: Faced state securities-fraud charges first filed in 2015; the case was resolved in 2024 via a pretrial agreement without a trial. Widely reported.

controversies.title: 2023 impeachment
controversies.detail: Impeached by the Texas House in 2023 over allegations of bribery and abuse of office; acquitted by the Texas Senate. He denied wrongdoing.

candidates.name: James Talarico
candidates.background: Texas state representative from Austin and former middle-school teacher; seminary student. Won the March 2026 Democratic primary.

cost.label: Authored $25/month insulin price-cap bill; campaign centers cost of living (Wikipedia)

health.label: Proposes 'Medicare for Y'all'. Medicare buy-in/public option for all (Wikipedia)

immigration.label: Border should be 'a giant welcome mat' with security; opposes border wall (Wikipedia)

safety.label: Authored Javier Ambler's Law and youth-justice reform bills (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Joined 2021 quorum break against voting restrictions; anti-gerrymandering, term limits, stock-trading ban (Wikipedia)

housing.label: Mixed: 'ban Wall Street from buying up housing stock' and expand LIHTC, and repeal 'outdated red tape' to build more (Talarico campaign)

taxes.label: Make 'giant corporations and the wealthiest Americans pay their fair share' to cut taxes for working families; raise corporate rates (Talarico campaign)

climate.label: Mixed: reinstate renewable tax credits and strengthen the Clean Air Act, while growing oil and gas jobs and cheaper gasoline (Talarico campaign)

repro.label: 'I've led the fight against efforts to ban abortion' (Ballotpedia)

candidates.name: Greg Abbott
candidates.background: Governor of Texas since 2015, seeking a fourth term; former Texas Attorney General. Won the March 2026 primary with 81.8%.

immigration.label: Launched Operation Lone Star; signed $1.54B border-barrier funding (Ballotpedia)

taxes.label: Supported Prop 4 (2023) property-tax cut and education-funding amendment (Ballotpedia)

climate.label: Sued the EPA to block greenhouse-gas regulation; opposed federal emissions rules (Ballotpedia)

education.label: Led the push for education savings accounts (vouchers), incl. primary campaigns against opponents (Ballotpedia)

democracy.label: Signed 2025 mid-decade congressional redistricting maps favoring his party (Ballotpedia)

cost.label: 'Taxes and Affordability': $18B 'largest property tax cut in Texas history,' ban capital-gains and inheritance taxes (Abbott campaign)

health.label: As AG, repeatedly sued to challenge the ACA: 'I go into the office in the morning, I sue Barack Obama' (Wikipedia)

housing.label: Signed SB 15, SB 840 and HB 24 cutting lot-size, parking and zoning barriers to boost housing supply (Office of the Texas Governor)

safety.label: 'Passed a law to prohibit cities from defunding the police'; bail package letting judges deny bail for violent crimes (Abbott campaign)

sources.label: Office of the Texas Governor: housing laws

candidates.name: Gina Hinojosa
candidates.background: Texas state representative from Austin; former Austin ISD school board president. Won the March 2026 Democratic primary with 58.5%.

cost.label: Campaign: corporations post record profits while Texans pay more; corporate accountability (Ballotpedia)

health.label: Campaign: rein in private equity and insurers 'making healthcare more expensive' (Ballotpedia)

taxes.label: Opposes tax incentives for 'private equity and corporate giants' (Ballotpedia)

education.label: Opposes Abbott's 'voucher scam'; invest in neighborhood public schools (Ballotpedia)

housing.label: Stop private equity 'from buying up housing'; 2025 bill capping institutional investors at 10 single-family homes (Hinojosa campaign)

repro.label: 'Stop the Republican assault on women's reproductive rights and restore funding to Planned Parenthood' (Ballotpedia)

democracy.label: Broke quorum in 2021 against voting-restriction bills and in 2025 against mid-decade redistricting (Wikipedia)

immigration.label: Voted nay on SB 4, the 2023 law making illegal entry a state crime enforceable with state deportation orders (Texas House Journal, Record 48)

climate.label: Voted nay on SB 2627, the Texas Energy Fund program of subsidized loans to build new gas power plants (Texas House Journal, Record 1977)

safety.label: Voted yea on SJR 5, the constitutional amendment requiring judges to deny bail for certain violent or sexual felonies, passed 133-8 (Texas House Journal, Record 2931)
